658	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
659	#
660	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
661	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
662	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
663	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
664	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
665	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
666	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
667	#
668	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
669	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
670	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
671	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
672	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
673	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
674	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
675	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
676	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
677	
678	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
679	_BREAKING = "breaking"
680	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
681	
682	# Witness recipe step tags (see ``_CompatDiffer``): an object field
683	# descent, one array-element nesting, a forced-kind leaf, and an omission
684	# of the innermost field.
685	_FIELD = "f"
686	_ARRAY = "a"
687	_KIND = "k"
688	_MISSING = "m"
689	
690	
691	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
692	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))
693	
694	
695	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
696	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
697	
698	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
699	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
700	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
701	    """
702	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
703	        return _BREAKING
704	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
705	        return _UNKNOWN
706	    return _COMPATIBLE

709	def _overflow_live(entry: dict) -> bool:
710	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
711	
712	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
713	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
714	    """
715	    names = entry.get("names", [])
716	    return names is None or bool(names)
717	
718	
719	def _overflow_routes(entry: dict | None, name: str) -> bool:
720	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
721	        return False
722	    names = entry.get("names")
723	    return names is None or name in names

726	class _CompatDiffer:
727	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""
728	
729	    def __init__(self) -> None:
730	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
731	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
732	        # One deterministic witness recipe per breaking pair position. Each
733	        # recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object to that
734	        # position, so a record can be built straight from a schema tree
735	        # without matching change strings, re-deriving the alignment, or
736	        # risking a collision between a real field name and a step token:
737	        # ``("f", name)`` descends through an object field, ``("a",)``
738	        # through one array element nesting, and the terminal step is
739	        # either ``("k", kind)`` (force a value of that kind) or
740	        # ``("m",)`` (omit the innermost field).
741	        self.recipes: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
742	        self._steps: list[tuple] = []
743	
744	    @contextlib.contextmanager
745	    def _step(self, step: tuple) -> Iterator[None]:
746	        self._steps.append(step)
747	        try:
748	            yield
749	        finally:
750	            self._steps.pop()
751	
752	    def witness(self, direction: str, terminal: tuple) -> None:
753	        """Record a witness recipe for one breaking pair position.
754	
755	        ``direction`` names the accepting (record) side for the breaking
756	        direction being witnessed (``"old"`` for a backward-breaking
757	        position, ``"new"`` for a forward-breaking one); ``terminal`` is
758	        the recipe's terminal step. Every call site is a non-collapsed
759	        exact branch the accepting side demonstrably accepts.
760	        """
761	        self.recipes.append((direction, tuple(self._steps) + (terminal,)))
762	
763	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
764	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
765	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
766	        return {
767	            "backward": backward,
768	            "forward": forward,
769	            "changes": self.changes,
770	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
771	        }
772	
773	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
774	        self.changes.append(
775	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
776	        )

778	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
779	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
780	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
781	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
782	            self.reasons.add(path)
783	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
784	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
785	        old_fields = old["fields"]
786	        new_fields = new["fields"]
787	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
788	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
789	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
790	            field_path = _join(path, name)
791	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
792	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
793	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
794	                with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
795	                    pair = self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
796	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
797	            elif old_entry is not None:
798	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
799	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
800	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
801	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
802	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
803	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
804	                else:
805	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
806	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
807	                    # under the forward direction.
808	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
809	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
810	                        # A legal new record omits it; the old
811	                        # required-field check reports it missing. That
812	                        # witness needs no value kind.
813	                        if not old_entry["optional"]:
814	                            self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
815	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(old_entry)
816	                        if kind is not None:
817	                            # A legal old record carries the field; new
818	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
819	                            self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
820	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
821	                        verdict,
822	                        (_BREAKING,
823	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
824	                    )
825	            else:
826	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
827	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
828	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
829	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
830	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
831	                else:
832	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
833	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
834	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
835	                    # carrying it unexpected.
836	                    self.change(
837	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
838	                    )
839	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
840	                        # A legal old record omits it; the new
841	                        # required-field check reports it missing.
842	                        if not new_entry["optional"]:
843	                            self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
844	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(new_entry)
845	                        if kind is not None:
846	                            # A legal new record carries the field; old
847	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
848	                            self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
849	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
850	                        verdict,
851	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
852	                         _BREAKING),
853	                    )
854	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
855	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
856	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
857	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
858	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
859	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
860	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
861	        return verdict

863	    @staticmethod
864	    def _witness_present_kind(entry: dict) -> str | None:
865	        """Deterministic kind a legal record uses for this exact entry.
866	
867	        Exact field entries compared here are never approximate, and a
868	        validated entry has observed at least one record, so its type set
869	        is non-empty. The fixed kind order (null, boolean, number, string,
870	        array, object) makes the choice independent of dict iteration
871	        order; scalars are preferred and an array precedes an object.
872	        """
873	        for kind in _KINDS:
874	            if kind in entry["types"]:
875	                return kind
876	        return None

878	    def compare_entry(
879	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
880	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
881	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
882	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
883	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
884	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
885	            self.reasons.add(path)
886	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
887	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
888	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
889	            if old["optional"]:
890	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it. The
891	                # field name is the current innermost step; the missing
892	                # witness omits exactly that field.
893	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
894	                self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
895	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
896	            else:
897	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
898	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
899	                self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
900	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
901	        verdict = _combine_pair(
902	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")
903	        )
904	        return verdict

906	    def compare_types(
907	        self, old_types: dict, new_types: dict, path: str, prefix: str
908	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
909	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
910	        for kind in _KINDS:
911	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
912	                continue
913	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
914	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)
915	            if old_node is not None and new_node is not None:
916	                verdict = _combine_pair(
917	                    verdict, self.compare_kind(old_node, new_node, path)
918	                )
919	            elif old_node is not None:
920	                # Records of this kind are legal on the old side but the
921	                # new type set no longer contains it (narrowing). A record
922	                # forcing exactly this kind is the backward witness.
923	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)
924	                self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
925	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
926	            else:
927	                # The new side widened with this kind; old check rejects
928	                # new records that take it (forward breaking), while old
929	                # records still pass the new, wider check.
930	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)
931	                self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
932	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
933	        return verdict

935	    def compare_kind(
936	        self, old_node: dict, new_node: dict, path: str
937	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
938	        kind = old_node["kind"]
939	        if kind in ("null", "boolean", "number", "string"):
940	            return _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
941	        if kind == "object":
942	            return self.compare_object(old_node, new_node, path)
943	        return self.compare_arrays(old_node, new_node, path)

945	    def compare_arrays(
946	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
947	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
948	        """Compare array element branches under one schema-level path.
949	
950	        check walks every element against the single merged element type
951	        set (a schema has no concrete indices), and it enforces that set
952	        even for a depth-capped array - only a collapsed *child* hides
953	        structure. So scalar element kinds gate exactly (rendered as
954	        ``path[]``) and collapsed element objects taint beneath them;
955	        element objects then join fields normally (``path[].name``). The
956	        matching array-level step marks the one nesting level check
957	        descends through per element.
958	        """
959	        element_path = f"{path}[]"
960	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
961	        for kind in _KINDS:
962	            if kind not in old["elements"] and kind not in new["elements"]:
963	                continue
964	            old_child = old["elements"].get(kind)
965	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)
966	            if old_child is not None and new_child is not None:
967	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
968	                    pair = self.compare_kind(old_child, new_child, element_path)
969	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
970	            elif old_child is not None:
971	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_removed", True)
972	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
973	                    self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
974	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
975	            else:
976	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_added", False)
977	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
978	                    self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
979	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
980	        return verdict

990	# -- breaking-change witnesses ----------------------------------------------
991	#
992	# A witness for a breaking direction is one JSON object that the accepting
993	# revision's ``check`` accepts (an empty report list) and the rejecting
994	# revision's ``check`` rejects (the full, non-empty report list). The
995	# differ records one recipe per breaking pair position while it walks; a
996	# recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object, and the builder
997	# below turns each into a concrete, deterministic record straight off the
998	# accepting revision's tree - it never parses change strings and never
999	# invents fields, kinds or values the accepting schema has not observed.
1000	# Required sibling fields are filled along the way so the record is legal
1001	# as a whole, not just at the breaking position; approximated branches are
1002	# never forced (a recipe can only end on a branch the differ proved), so
1003	# an ``unknown`` direction simply yields no witness.
1004	
1005	# Canonical, deterministic leaf values. Booleans and numbers stay
1006	# distinct kinds (``True`` is never used where a number is required), and
1007	# ``None`` is only produced for the explicit null kind, never for a
1008	# missing field.
1009	_WITNESS_VALUES = {
1010	    "null": None,
1011	    "boolean": True,
1012	    "number": 1,
1013	    "string": "x",
1014	}
1015	
1016	
1017	def _check_against(root: dict, record: Any) -> list[str]:
1018	    """Run the exact ``check`` pipeline against an in-memory root."""
1019	    reports: list[str] = []

1089	def _witness_value(types: dict, recipe: tuple, index: int) -> tuple[Any, int]:
1090	    """Build the value at one field/element position from ``recipe``.
1091	
1092	    ``types`` is the accepting side's type set at that position and
1093	    ``index`` points at the next step. Returns the value and the index of
1094	    the consumed terminal step.
1095	    """
1096	    tag, *payload = recipe[index]
1097	    if tag == _ARRAY:
1098	        # One nesting level: check walks every element against the one
1099	        # merged element set, so a single element witnesses the branch.
1100	        node = types["array"]
1101	        element, terminal = _witness_value(node["elements"], recipe, index + 1)
1102	        return [element], terminal
1103	    if tag == _FIELD:
1104	        node = types["object"]
1105	        return _witness_object_field(node, recipe, index)
1106	    # Terminal forced kind.
1107	    assert tag == _KIND
1108	    return _complete_value(types, payload[0]), index

1114	    """Build an object value, forcing the recipe's field within it."""
1115	    tag, name = recipe[index]
1116	    assert tag == _FIELD
1117	    record: dict[str, Any] = {}
1118	    next_index = index + 1
1119	    next_step = recipe[next_index]
1120	    if next_step[0] == _MISSING:
1121	        # The witness omits this field, which the accepting tree may not
1122	        # even track (a field the other side removed or only it requires);
1123	        # only required siblings are filled.
1124	        _fill_required(node, record, name)
1125	        return record, next_index
1126	    entry = node["fields"][name]
1127	    value, terminal = _witness_value(entry["types"], recipe, next_index)
1128	    record[name] = value
1129	    _fill_required(node, record, name)
1130	    return record, terminal

1140	def _witness_report(
1141	    old_revision: int, new_revision: int, old_root: dict, new_root: dict
1142	) -> dict:
1143	    """The compat report plus verifiable breaking-direction witnesses."""
1144	    differ = _CompatDiffer()
1145	    report = differ.diff(old_root, new_root)
1146	    witnesses: dict[str, Any] = {"backward": None, "forward": None}
1147	    for direction, verdict, accepting, rejecting, side in (
1148	        ("backward", report["backward"], old_root, new_root, "old"),
1149	        ("forward", report["forward"], new_root, old_root, "new"),
1150	    ):
1151	        if verdict != _BREAKING:
1152	            # A compatible direction has no counterexample; an unknown
1153	            # direction cannot be settled, so one must never be forged.
1154	            continue
1155	        chosen: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1156	        for recipe_side, recipe in differ.recipes:
1157	            if recipe_side != side:
1158	                continue
1159	            record = _witness_record(accepting, recipe)
1160	            accepted_reports = _check_against(accepting, record)
1161	            rejected_reports = _check_against(rejecting, record)
1162	            if not accepted_reports and rejected_reports:
1163	                chosen = {"record": record, "reports": rejected_reports}
1164	                break
1165	        # Every breaking verdict comes from at least one exact breaking
1166	        # pair position, whose recipe must verify through check itself.
1167	        if chosen is None:  # pragma: no cover - construction invariant
1168	            raise SchemaConflict("could not construct a verifiable witness")
1169	        witnesses[direction] = chosen
1170	    return {
1171	        "from": old_revision,
1172	        "to": new_revision,
1173	        **report,
1174	        "witnesses": witnesses,
1175	    }

1178	# -- field migration preview -------------------------------------------------
1179	#
1180	# A migration rule is a small JSON object describing one field-level edit:
1181	# ``{"op": "rename", "path": [...], "to": name}`` moves a field's value to
1182	# a new sibling name, ``{"op": "drop", "path": [...]}`` removes a field,
1183	# and ``{"op": "default", "path": [...], "value": ...}`` fills a field that
1184	# is genuinely missing (a present ``null`` is a value and is kept). The
1185	# path is a non-empty array whose string segments are literal field names
1186	# (a name containing a dot names one field, never a descent) and whose
1187	# ``null`` segments select every element of the array at that position;
1188	# the last segment is always a string naming the field the op edits.
1189	# Rules apply in order, each to the result of the previous one. A parent
1190	# that is simply missing skips the rule for that branch - parents are
1191	# never created - while a string segment meeting a non-object or a null
1192	# segment meeting a non-array is a structural ``ValueError``, as is a
1193	# rename whose target field already exists.
1194	
1195	_MIGRATION_OPS = ("rename", "drop", "default")
1196

1198	def _require_json_value(value: Any, what: str) -> None:
1199	    """Reject anything JSON cannot represent, recursing into containers."""
1200	    if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool, int)):
1201	        return
1202	    if isinstance(value, float):
1203	        if math.isfinite(value):
1204	            return
1205	    elif isinstance(value, list):
1206	        for item in value:
1207	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1208	        return
1209	    elif isinstance(value, dict):
1210	        for key, item in value.items():
1211	            if not isinstance(key, str):
1212	                break
1213	            _require_json_value(item, what)
1214	        else:
1215	            return
1216	    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a JSON value")

1219	def _parse_migration_rules(rules: Any) -> list[dict]:
1220	    """Validate the rule list structurally before anything is applied.
1221	
1222	    Every rule must be a JSON object carrying exactly the keys its op
1223	    needs - ``op`` and ``path`` for all three, ``to`` for rename,
1224	    ``value`` for default - with a non-empty path of string/null segments
1225	    ending in a string, a string rename target distinct from the source
1226	    field name, and a JSON default value. Anything else is a
1227	    ``ValueError`` raised before any revision is read or any rule runs.
1228	    """
1229	    if not isinstance(rules, list):
1230	        raise ValueError("migration rules must be a JSON array")
1231	    for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
1232	        if not isinstance(rule, dict):
1233	            raise ValueError(f"migration rule {index} must be a JSON object")
1234	        op = rule.get("op")
1235	        if op not in _MIGRATION_OPS:
1236	            raise ValueError(f"migration rule {index}: unknown op {op!r}")
1237	        path = rule.get("path")
1238	        if (
1239	            not isinstance(path, list)
1240	            or not path
1241	            or any(
1242	                segment is not None and not isinstance(segment, str)
1243	                for segment in path
1244	            )
1245	            or not isinstance(path[-1], str)
1246	        ):
1247	            raise ValueError(f"migration rule {index}: invalid path")
1248	        expected = {"op", "path"}
1249	        if op == "rename":
1250	            expected.add("to")
1251	        elif op == "default":
1252	            expected.add("value")
1253	        if set(rule) != expected:
1254	            raise ValueError(f"migration rule {index}: invalid keys for {op}")
1255	        if op == "rename":
1256	            if not isinstance(rule["to"], str):
1257	                raise ValueError(
1258	                    f"migration rule {index}: rename target must be a string"
1259	                )
1260	            if rule["to"] == path[-1]:
1261	                raise ValueError(
1262	                    f"migration rule {index}: rename target equals the "
1263	                    "source field"
1264	                )
1265	        elif op == "default":
1266	            _require_json_value(rule["value"], f"migration rule {index} value")
1267	    return rules

1270	def _migration_containers(record: dict, path: list) -> list:
1271	    """The containers the path's final segment applies to.
1272	
1273	    Navigates every segment but the last: a string segment descends into
1274	    the named field of an object (a missing field drops that branch
1275	    silently - parents are never created), a null segment spreads over
1276	    every element of an array (an empty array simply selects nothing).
1277	    A string segment meeting a non-object or a null segment meeting a
1278	    non-array is a structural ``ValueError``.
1279	    """
1280	    containers = [record]
1281	    for segment in path[:-1]:
1282	        following = []
1283	        for container in containers:
1284	            if segment is None:
1285	                if not isinstance(container, list):
1286	                    raise ValueError("null path segment requires an array")
1287	                following.extend(container)
1288	            else:
1289	                if not isinstance(container, dict):
1290	                    raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1291	                if segment in container:
1292	                    following.append(container[segment])
1293	        if not following:
1294	            return []
1295	        containers = following
1296	    return containers

1299	def _apply_migration_rule(record: dict, rule: dict) -> None:
1300	    """Apply one already-validated rule to the working record in place."""
1301	    op = rule["op"]
1302	    last = rule["path"][-1]
1303	    for container in _migration_containers(record, rule["path"]):
1304	        if not isinstance(container, dict):
1305	            raise ValueError("string path segment requires an object")
1306	        if op == "rename":
1307	            if last not in container:
1308	                continue
1309	            to = rule["to"]
1310	            if to in container:
1311	                raise ValueError(f"rename target {to!r} already exists")
1312	            # Rebuild in place so the field keeps its position under the
1313	            # new name and the same input always yields the same order.
1314	            renamed = [
1315	                (to if key == last else key, value)
1316	                for key, value in container.items()
1317	            ]
1318	            container.clear()
1319	            container.update(renamed)
1320	        elif op == "drop":
1321	            container.pop(last, None)
1322	        # default fills only a genuinely missing field; a present null is
1323	        # a value and is never replaced.
1324	        elif last not in container:
1325	            container[last] = copy.deepcopy(rule["value"])

1457	def _write_atomic(file_path: Path, text: str) -> None:
1458	    """Write text atomically: a crash leaves only the old or new file."""
1459	    tmp = file_path.with_name(file_path.name + ".tmp")
1460	    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
1461	    try:
1462	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1463	            handle.write(text)
1464	            handle.flush()
1465	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1466	        os.replace(tmp, file_path)
1467	    except BaseException:
1468	        try:
1469	            os.unlink(tmp)
1470	        except OSError:
1471	            pass
1472	        raise
1473	    _fsync_dir(file_path.parent)
